question_change_record.previous_question: Finerenone across kidney and cardiovascular outcomes, as previously published
question_change_record.why_not_answerable: The previous page pooled FIDELIO-DKD's KIDNEY primary (kidney failure, sustained eGFR decline, renal death) with FIGARO-DKD's CARDIOVASCULAR primary, and added FINEARTS-HF, a heart-failure population rather than a CKD one, plus a record whose registry id had been nulled. Those are different questions in different populations and no single estimate answers them.
question_change_record.what_changed: Restricted to FIDELIO-DKD and FIGARO-DKD on the CARDIOVASCULAR composite, which is FIGARO's primary outcome and FIDELIO's key secondary, and which both trials define with the same four components.
question_change_record.supersedes: the earlier FINERENONE_REVIEW page, archived and not deleted

cv_composite_first.poolable_DEPRECATED_note: `poolable` MEANT ONLY 'the source page pooled these trials'. It was never a judgement that the pool was sound, and the renderer read it as permission to assert 'pooled on the X scale'. RENAMED to source_page_pooled, which is what it says. `poolable` is retained so nothing breaks, and it is DEPRECATED: read source_page_pooled for what the source did, and estimand_established for whether the pool is defensible. A PAGE SHOULD DISPLAY A POOLED ESTIMATE BECAUSE ITS ESTIMAND WAS ESTABLISHED, NOT BECAUSE SOMEONE ONCE POOLED IT.
cv_composite_first.estimand_established_means: TRUE only where every contributing trial has been READ and shown to measure the same quantity, or the same construct with a variance stated. FALSE where that was checked and failed. NULL where it was never checked -- AN ABSENT ASSERTION AND A NEGATIVE ONE ARE DIFFERENT STATES and null is not a pass.

house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.estimator: REML with Hartung-Knapp, t on k-1 = 1 degree(s) of freedom (t = 12.7062)
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.THE_POINT_ESTIMATE_IS_UNCHANGED: The published point is 0.8655 and the house-rule point is 0.8655. THE NUMBER A READER REMEMBERS DOES NOT MOVE; what differs is the precision claim. That is why nothing downstream catches this -- every memorable quantity survives.

published_interval.restated_2026_08_20: The published interval is now REML, so this block compares a REML point interval against a REML Hartung-Knapp one and the ESTIMATOR is no longer one of the things that differ between them. At k=2 the moment estimator and REML coincide exactly, so not one digit of this block's numbers moved -- only the label, which was wrong.

house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.variance_inflation_floor: A FLOOR OF 1 IS APPLIED TO THE VARIANCE-INFLATION FACTOR so the adjustment can never NARROW an interval below the unadjusted one. That guard is the recognised modification for exactly this instability, and its existence is evidence the small-k behaviour is a KNOWN problem with KNOWN handling rather than a novel judgement.
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.no_rule_is_decided_here: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-20. The rule WAS decided, in DECISIONS-COCHRANE-2026-08-18.md section 1, and applied on 2026-08-20: REML is the estimator corpus-wide, and Hartung-Knapp is a SENSITIVITY analysis at k<=3 rather than the primary interval (Handbook 6.5 s10.10.4.4-10.10.4.5). Both intervals still stand on this page and nothing is unpublished.
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.what_this_means_for_this_pool: THE PUBLISHED INTERVAL EXCLUDES 1 AND THE HOUSE-RULE INTERVAL CROSSES IT. A SIGNIFICANCE VERDICT TURNS ON THE INTERVAL METHOD ALONE. A reader shown only the published interval has been told something firmer than the evidence supports; a reader shown only the wider one loses that the contributing trials agree. BOTH ARE HERE.
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.read_the_width_with_care: AT k=2 HARTUNG-KNAPP USES t ON ONE DEGREE OF FREEDOM -- 12.7062 against the normal 1.9600 -- and the interval is enormously wider. That width is a property of the method at very few studies, not a measurement of this evidence. It is recorded so a reader can see it; it is NOT presented as the better interval.

r_output.what_it_is: The fit that produces the numbers this block now publishes, printed by metafor and pasted unaltered. The previous fit, under the estimator this pool used before 2026-08-20, is kept beside it under r_output_superseded_2026_08_20 rather than discarded.
r_output.reproduction_of_the_previous_value: Before this refit was applied, the OLD estimator was refitted on the same inputs and checked against the stored value: REPRODUCED. A pool whose old fit did not reproduce was not overwritten.

cv_composite_first.estimator_note_2026_08_18_superseded_202: Published as DerSimonian-Laird. The house-rule interval is recorded alongside rather than replacing it, so the difference is visible instead of silently resolved.
cv_composite_first.estimator_note_2026_08_20: REML, applied 2026-08-20 under DECISIONS-COCHRANE-2026-08-18.md section 1, on Cochrane Handbook 6.5 section 10.10.4.4: "Decision: REML, everywhere." The estimator this pool used before that date was DerSimonian-Laird; that fit was reproduced first and is quoted under r_output_superseded_2026_08_20, so the movement is attributable rather than asserted.

display_change_announced.what_changed: `heterogeneity.i2` and `heterogeneity.tau2` are field names that each map to more than one standard definition. Every number is unchanged; each now carries the definition it holds. tau2's definition was already recoverable from the declared `estimator` beside it and is copied, never inferred. i2's was not recoverable and is DECIDED BY RECOMPUTING BOTH FORMS from this object's own per-trial inputs, with the evidence recorded.
display_change_announced.why: A reader recomputing Higgins I-squared from the Q printed beside it would have concluded the object was wrong -- and would have been behaving exactly as we want readers to behave. An ambiguous label on an unambiguous number is a defect specifically against the only reader we claim to serve.

display_change_announced.change: estimator changed to REML -- LABEL ONLY, no value moved
display_change_announced.what_changed: This pool was fitted with DerSimonian-Laird. It is refitted with REML under DECISIONS-COCHRANE-2026-08-18.md section 1, on Cochrane Handbook 6.5 section 10.10.4.4: "Decision: REML, everywhere." The old fit was reproduced against the stored value FIRST (REPRODUCED) and only then replaced. Stored values are also rounded at storage -- effects to 4 decimals, tau-squared and Q to 6, I-squared to 4 -- because several of these pools carried sixteen significant figures on a two- or three-study pool.
display_change_announced.why: The corpus held two estimator conventions at once: 23 pools REML, 9 DerSimonian-Laird, 1 Paule-Mandel. Handbook 6.5 s10.10.4.4 records REML as RevMan's own current default and this project's statistics rules already refused DerSimonian-Laird below k=10, which every pool in this corpus is. The decision was taken on 2026-08-18 and not applied; applying it to some pools and not others would have been worse than either convention.

provenance_verified_2026_08_18: Provenance written ONLY where the registry confirmed it. Every statement on this object names the outcome measure its counts were matched against and the date of the comparison. Trials whose registration posts no results carry an explicit NOT SUPPLIED BY THE REGISTRY note with the source question recorded as owed.
